headline: Pricing and cost discipline lift margins despite soft volume
summary_short: Reynolds Consumer Products' Q2 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026) revenue rose 0.6% y/y to $944 million as pricing actions offset lower volume, while net income climbed 21.9% to $89 million and diluted EPS rose to $0.42 from $0.35.
summary_long: Revenue grew $6 million to $944 million on higher pricing versus input costs, partly offset by lower volume. Cost of sales fell 2% to $699 million on lower operational costs, expanding gross margin to 25.95% from 24.10%. Operating income rose 16.9% to $138 million despite an 11% SG&A increase. Net income rose 21.9% to $89 million and diluted EPS to $0.42, helped by the non-repeat of prior-year CEO-transition and strategic-initiative costs. Segment mix was uneven: Home & Tableware Adjusted EBITDA rose 23%, while Storage & Organization fell 10% on new-business ramp costs. Cash fell to $66 million after a $50 million debt repayment and $101 million of capex; a $0.23/share dividend was declared. No forward guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Increase was primarily due to higher pricing in response to higher input costs and the timing of promotional activity, partially offset by lower volume.
Cost of sales fell $13 million (2%) to $699 million, primarily driven by lower operational costs and lower volume, while revenue held flat to up.
Fully explained by cost of sales falling 2% while revenue rose slightly, per the disclosed revenue and cost-of-sales lines above.
Follows from higher gross profit, partly offset by SG&A rising $11 million (11%) on higher personnel, professional-fee and advertising costs.
Company's own Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP, $171M this quarter) rose 5% y/y, driven by lower operational costs, partially offset by lower volume and higher SG&A.
Net income increased, primarily driven by lower operational costs; the prior-year quarter also carried CEO-transition and strategic-initiative costs that did not repeat.
Tracks the net-income gain; diluted share count rose only slightly (211.9M from 210.3M), so per-share growth ran a bit below the net-income growth rate.
Pricing actions and lower operational costs drove margin expansion and a 22% three-month net-income gain even as volume stayed soft across most segments.
